title: Why Your Contractor Website Isn't Converting (And How to Fix It)
meta: Around 98% of contractor-website visitors leave without calling. The four fixes: phone number up top, outcomes not services, proof on page one, and a load under 3 seconds.
short: About 98% of your website visitors leave without calling — usually for four fixable reasons: no phone number up top, services instead of outcomes, no proof, and a slow load.
statLabel: Of contractor-website visitors leave without contacting you (WebFX 2026)

body.h2: No phone number above the fold
body.answer: If they hunt for it, they call a competitor.
body.html: Around 98% of visitors leave without contacting you (WebFX 2026). The number-one fix is the number itself — big, tappable, above the fold on every page.

body.answer: Homeowners buy 'cool house by Friday,' not 'HVAC installation.'
body.html: Lead with the outcome the homeowner wants, not the industry term. 'AC fixed today' beats 'HVAC installation and repair services' every time.

body.answer: Trust on page one; load under 3 seconds.
body.html: Reviews, job photos, and faces on page one carry the sale. And speed is a conversion feature — 3 seconds to load or you lose half your visitors before they see any of it.

faq.q: Why isn't my contractor website getting leads?
faq.a: Usually four reasons: the phone number is hard to find, you list services instead of outcomes, there's no proof (reviews/photos), and it loads slowly. ~98% of visitors leave without contacting you (WebFX 2026).

faq.q: What's the most important thing on a contractor website?
faq.a: A visible, tappable phone number above the fold on every page — plus proof (reviews and job photos) on the first screen.

faq.q: How fast should my website load?
faq.a: Under 3 seconds. Slower than that and roughly half your visitors leave before they see your offer — speed is a booking feature.
